investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Eval Failing: POST /api/agents Returns 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit is 100)
investigation.summary: The AURA observability eval for remote-agent-create (and all sibling checks remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-15T22:12:59Z because POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with the error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval probe never received a successful agent creation response, so zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were collected and all contract assertions went unverified. This is an eval-layer failure reflecting a real API-level quota enforcement condition; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet to confirm a broader production outage.
investigation.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend rejected the eval's POST /api/agents request with a 409 Conflict because the org used by the observability probe has reached or exceeded the remote agent quota limit of 100. The createAgent call in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1258) propagated this error before any evidence could be written, causing all three remote-agents checks to fail with the identical message. The quota condition is the earliest violated boundary; the eval infrastructure itself is functioning correctly (the request was made and a structured error was returned within 1322 ms, well under the 120 000 ms outage threshold).

sibling.remote-agent-state and sibling.remote-agent-runtime: both siblings carry the identical 409 message (sameMessage: true), indicating the shared createAgent upstream call is the single point of failure for all three checks.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Org-level remote agent quota exhausted: the probe org already has 100 remote agents registered in the swarm backend. The API enforces a hard limit of 100 and returns 409 on any further creation attempt. All three checks share the same createAgent call path, explaining the identical failure message across remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime.

SECONDARY — Leaked or un-cleaned eval agents from prior runs: the withCleanup wrapper (run-status-probes.mjs line 1256) is responsible for deleting agents after each probe run. If a previous run crashed or cleanup was skipped (e.g., due to an earlier error or a process kill), agents may have accumulated in the probe org over time, eventually hitting the 100-agent ceiling.

TERTIARY — Probe org misconfiguration: the observability probe may be running against an org that is shared with non-eval workloads or that has a lower effective quota than expected, causing the limit to be reached sooner than anticipated.

LOW CONFIDENCE — Regression introduced by d58f85f: commit d58f85f touched eval runner files (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, features.json, check-expectations.json) approximately 2 hours before the failure. However, the suspect-change confidence is rated low, the commit's touched paths do not include any candidate code paths that match the failing needles, and the 409 error is a backend quota signal, not a runner logic error. This hypothesis is not supported by the current eval evidence.

investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed immediately with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying HTTP 404, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint targeted by the eval runner was not reachable at the time of the run. investigation.rootCause: The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1357) issued an SSE request to /api/generate/image/stream, which internally attempted to open an agent runtime session. The agent runtime responded with HTTP 404, surfaced as SESSION_OPEN_FAILED. This terminated the stream before any generation_completed frame or image URL could be produced, making it impossible to satisfy the required evidence assertions (frameTypes contains generation_completed; imageUrlPresent equals true). The failure is localized to the production-api runtime environment and to this specific eval check; no sibling checks failed and no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so this is an eval-infrastructure failure, not a confirmed user-facing outage. The most likely proximate cause is that the agent runtime harness endpoint was absent, misconfigured, or running an incompatible version at the time the eval executed — consistent with the error message text and the 404 status.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Eval Failing: POST /api/agents Returns 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit is 100)
investigations.summary: The AURA observability eval for remote-agent-create (and all sibling checks remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-15T22:12:59Z because POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with the error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval probe never received a successful agent creation response, so zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were collected and all contract assertions went unverified. This is an eval-layer failure reflecting a real API-level quota enforcement condition; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet to confirm a broader production outage.
investigations.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend rejected the eval's POST /api/agents request with a 409 Conflict because the org used by the observability probe has reached or exceeded the remote agent quota limit of 100. The createAgent call in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1258) propagated this error before any evidence could be written, causing all three remote-agents checks to fail with the identical message. The quota condition is the earliest violated boundary; the eval infrastructure itself is functioning correctly (the request was made and a structured error was returned within 1322 ms, well under the 120 000 ms outage threshold).

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Org-level remote agent quota exhausted: the probe org already has 100 remote agents registered in the swarm backend. The API enforces a hard limit of 100 and returns 409 on any further creation attempt. All three checks share the same createAgent call path, explaining the identical failure message across remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime.

SECONDARY — Leaked or un-cleaned eval agents from prior runs: the withCleanup wrapper (run-status-probes.mjs line 1256) is responsible for deleting agents after each probe run. If a previous run crashed or cleanup was skipped (e.g., due to an earlier error or a process kill), agents may have accumulated in the probe org over time, eventually hitting the 100-agent ceiling.

TERTIARY — Probe org misconfiguration: the observability probe may be running against an org that is shared with non-eval workloads or that has a lower effective quota than expected, causing the limit to be reached sooner than anticipated.

LOW CONFIDENCE — Regression introduced by d58f85f: commit d58f85f touched eval runner files (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, features.json, check-expectations.json) approximately 2 hours before the failure. However, the suspect-change confidence is rated low, the commit's touched paths do not include any candidate code paths that match the failing needles, and the 409 error is a backend quota signal, not a runner logic error. This hypothesis is not supported by the current eval evidence.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) — Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable in production-api Environment
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed immediately with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying HTTP 404, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint targeted by the eval runner was not reachable at the time of the run. Because the session could not be opened, no SSE frames beyond generation_start were emitted, leaving both required evidence keys (frameTypes, imageUrlPresent) entirely absent and causing the expected-output contract to fail.
investigations.rootCause: The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1357) issued an SSE request to /api/generate/image/stream, which internally attempted to open an agent runtime session. The agent runtime responded with HTTP 404, surfaced as SESSION_OPEN_FAILED. This terminated the stream before any generation_completed frame or image URL could be produced, making it impossible to satisfy the required evidence assertions (frameTypes contains generation_completed; imageUrlPresent equals true). The failure is localized to the production-api runtime environment and to this specific eval check; no sibling checks failed and no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so this is an eval-infrastructure failure, not a confirmed user-facing outage. The most likely proximate cause is that the agent runtime harness endpoint was absent, misconfigured, or running an incompatible version at the time the eval executed — consistent with the error message text and the 404 status.
